text: In 2017, the Region of Niagara and the Iroquois Caucus condemned a plan to transport 23,000 litres of liquid radioactive waste over public roads and bridges. A plan that would have seen hazardous material being transported through the Greater Toronto Area, over and around waterways that lead to Lake Ontario, Toronto’s drinking water supply, putting public and environmental health at risk. The Great Lakes basin itself provides drinking water to 40 million people in the United States and Canada. More worrisome is that it is unclear whether Toronto’s first responders are made aware of materials that are transported through the Greater Toronto Area. At minimum, there needs to be full transparency with local first responders about what and when materials are being transported through a jurisdiction.

City Council on July 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 30, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Office of Emergency Management, in consultation with the Medical Officer of Health, to report on the risk of liquid radioactive waste travelling in the Greater Toronto Area, specifically, the transportation of highly enriched uranium from Chalk River Laboratories into the United States.
